top.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
top.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. top.description: Bayern star leaves France camp following Italy defeat Bayern Munich centre-back Dayot Upamecano has departed the French national team camp. The French Football Federation confirmed on Friday that the 28-year-old has left the camp early for personal reasons. top.description: India's lowest ODI totals: Listing down Men in Blue's worst-ever performances in One-day cricket originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India’s batting has suffered painful collapses on tours of New Zealand over the decades. India’s all-time lowest ODI total is far smaller than many fans might expect. A full list across all Test nations shows just how rare such collapses are. What is India's lowest score in ODI cricket? Full list of Men in Blue's worst totals India’s lowest ODI totals make for uncomfortable reading, even for a side that has won two World Cups and built a reputation for some of the most fearless batting in white-ball cricket. Every team has its bad days, but the scorecards below show that India’s worst afternoons came in a few clear patterns, most often against the swinging ball and on pitches that offered the bowlers more than they could handle. New Zealand has been one of the toughest places for those collapses to happen. India’s lowest ODI total on New Zealand soil is 92, a score recorded at Seddon Park in Hamilton on January 31, 2019, when the visitors were bowled out in 30.5 overs. Trent Boult was the destroyer that day with figures of 5 for 21, and Rohit Sharma, who was leading the side in his 200th ODI, could only watch as the innings fell apart. However, that Hamilton collapse wasn’t the first time the team had struggled badly in New Zealand. The 2002-03 tour remains the darkest period, as four of India’s five lowest totals in the country came on that single trip, and the hosts won the seven-match series 5-2. Two innings ended on 108, and two more finished on 122, which is why that tour is still remembered with a shudder. Across all countries, India have been bowled out for fewer than 100 on seven occasions, and the lowest of them all is 54 against Sri Lanka in Sharjah in 2000. Four of the entries come from the 2002-03 tour, including the 108 at Eden Park in Auckland in the opening match, where New Zealand won by three wickets. The 108 at Christchurch on January 1, 2003 followed, and the two 122s came at Queenstown and Hamilton. The older entries show how long the problem goes back. The 138 at Dunedin in March 1990 was India’s opening match in a triangular series, and the 154 and 156 totals from February 1976 came in the first ODIs the two teams ever played in New Zealand. Those games were played with eight-ball overs, which is why the overs column shows “8-ball” for them. India lost the first one by nine wickets and the second by 80 runs. The 153 at Hamilton in February 1981 left India well short of a New Zealand total of 210, and the 149 at Auckland in March 2009 came in a series that India still won 3-1. top.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
top.description: Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday [Getty Images] As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," one woman watching the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news [BBC] Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. There's a sense of injustice that Australia can't escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story [Getty Images] Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. top.title: US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy
top.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote Thursday on X. Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. – Informal Trump adviser – Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. top.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
top.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. top.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. top.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
top.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

top.description: ORCHARD PARK - If there was a moment when the team-wide frustration that the New York Jets have experienced this season boiled to a head, it was last Sunday in Kansas City when quarterback Geno Smith momentarily lost his mind. In the second quarter of what became their fourth straight loss, the Jets were leading 9-7 when Braelon Allen lost a fumble that was recovered by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman. As Gilman began his return, Smith rushed over and launched himself with intent and knocked Gilman flat at the Jets 24, a stunning display of physicality from a quarterback. “It's something that you really don't want to happen, but competitors are going to compete, so I'm not surprised that it happened, but that's something that you don't want from your starting quarterback,” coach Aaron Glenn said. Smith knew the fumble was a huge mistake and sure enough, the Chiefs scored two plays later and grabbed a lead they never relinquished in their 35-12 blowout. Later in the game, following another failed Jets possession, Smith came to the sideline and slammed his helmet to the ground, the inevitability of falling to 2-7 clearly getting to him. As usual in mid-November, the Jets are already in playing-out-the-string mode, but they have a great chance to make a statement Sunday when they host the 7-1 Buffalo Bills . There isn’t too much left to play for downstate, but beating the AFC’s No. 1 team and damaging the Bills’ quest for the No. 1 seed would certainly provide some professional joy, especially considering the two 30-10 and 35-8 beatings Buffalo put on New York last year. “We're not going to hide from the fact that we're 2-7,” said Glenn, who is likely coaching for his job so every possible victory is crucial. “We own that, but man, we're still working our (butts) off to make sure we fix that. We like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that. When you look at the seven losses, and this is just the facts, five of the teams were playoff-caliber teams. top.description: Atletico Madrid v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/2027 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona midfielder Gavi has no intention of leaving the Catalan giants despite attracting transfer interest from European heavyweights Bayern Munich and Napoli. Although the 22-year-old Spain international has struggled for regular starts this season, he remains determined to stay at Camp Nou and win back his place in the starting line-up. Midfielder rules out Camp Nou exit Reports from Marca reveal that the idea of departing Catalonia has never "crossed the player's mind", while sporting director Deco has zero desire to sanction a sale. Both the 22-year-old's camp and club hierarchy insist his future is completely secure despite recent enquiries from Italy and Germany. Having made 175 senior appearances since joining La Masia from Real Betis in 2015, the academy graduate wants to stay put. Fierce competition limits starting opportunities Gavi has been restricted to just 229 minutes across nine appearances this term - comprising five La Liga outings and four in the Champions League - with only two of those coming as a starter. Head coach Hansi Flick currently favours a first-choice double pivot of Pedri and Rodri, while youngster Marc Bernal has served as the primary deputy whenever either is unavailable, including during last weekend's victory away at Atletico Madrid. Pathways further forward are similarly congested for the versatile Andalusian. Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo currently share the attacking midfield duties, while Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi rotate on the left flank. Strong bond underpins mutual confidence Even though the Spanish publication notes that the midfielder is "not happy with his role", his motivation remains high and he stays "confident" of earning more minutes as the campaign progresses. His limited involvement has not affected his "close relationship" with Flick, who admires the player's relentless character and footballing ability. Gavi even views the German tactician as a father figure, a bond highlighted when the pair shared a warm embrace on the touchline after sealing victory at the Metropolitano last weekend . Demanding winter schedule promises rotation With Barcelona facing a packed and demanding fixture list after the November international break, Flick is expected to rotate his squad far more frequently over the coming months. That congested calendar should hand Gavi regular opportunities to challenge Pedri, Rodri and Bernal for a starting berth in the engine room. Consequently, the Spain international will ignore any January approaches from Bayern or Napoli to focus entirely on his Camp Nou career.

top.title: Nick Sanchez Returns To Win Mode With McAnally-Hilgemann
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Nick Sanchez is back where he belongs, driving the No. 18 truck for McAnally-Hilgemann Racing in the 2027 NASCAR Truck Series. The team made the official announcement on Thursday, November 12, ending months of uncertainty for the young driver. Sanchez will chase his second championship title with a stable that already knows how to win big. The Sanchez move puts a proven winner behind the wheel. The driver wasted no time in sharing his thoughts on the new ride. “This is a tremendous opportunity to join MHR and compete full time again at a high level”, Sanchez said, according to Motorsport.com . He knows the road ahead will be tough, but he feels ready to handle the pressure. After a year of jumping between part-time seats, he has a clear plan for the upcoming season. A Fresh Start After a Rough Year Sanchez did not have the smoothest ride in 2026. He started the year with Am Racing, but that team shut down abruptly. He then drove for the Peterson Racing Group in various races while making four starts with Spire Motorsports. That kind of instability can wear a driver down, but Sanchez kept his focus. With two victories, eight pole positions, and 14 top-five finishes, he has made 51 previous starts in the Truck Series. Those numbers prove he can handle the competition. Team owner Bill McAnally sees the value in bringing Sanchez home. “We’re ecstatic to have Nick in the fold with us”, team owner Bill McAnally said. The owner believes the driver’s raw speed will lift the whole operation. He wants to see Sanchez turn his talent into more race results next year. The team is hungry for a title, and adding a winner like Sanchez gives them a real shot at getting it. The connection between Sanchez and McAnally-Hilgemann goes back a long way. Sanchez has won at every level throughout his career, including victories at Daytona and Charlotte in 2024. He also won at Atlanta in the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series in 2025. McAnally-Hilgemann Racing has the cars and the crew to support that kind of talent. Together, they have a good chance to dominate the 2027 season. Sanchez mentioned in his statement that he has a ton of energy and excitement for what’s ahead. He thanked Bill McAnally, Chevrolet, and everyone involved at MHR for making the deal happen. The driver is looking forward to the first race in February.

top.title: Russia threatens hosts Germany if banned from men's ice hockey worlds
top.description: FILE PHOTO - The players of the USA (L) and Canada warm up before the start of the men's ice hockey match between Canada and USA during the 2026 Olympic Winter Games Milan Cortina. Ice hockey games at the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps could be moved to Paris or Lyon because the new mayor of Nice opposes a temporary venue in the home stadium of a local football club. (is associated with: «Russia threatens hosts Germany if banned from men's ice hockey worlds») Peter Kneffel/dpa Russia's ice hockey federation has threatened host nation Germany with compensation claims should it be banned from the men's 2027 world championships. A corresponding application has already been submitted to the ethics committee of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Russian federation president Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency. This comes amid the heated debate surrounding the reinstatement of Russia to international competition by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and the subsequent threat of boycott of the tournament from several nations and also sponsors. Canada, host of the men's world junior ice hockey championships at the end of the year, announced it will not grant visas to Russian players. In Germany, the federal government declared that hosting the tournament would be "virtually impossible" if Russia participated. "Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Tretiak said after a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and other sports officials. Several countries, including world champions Finland, have stated they will not compete against Russian teams. The Finnish and the Norwegian governments also announced this week that they will not issue visas to Russian athletes. The restrictions will initially have the greatest impact on winter sports, with a number of competitions taking place in Finland and Norway.

Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. nigeria.title: ‘Years of injustice’ fuel northern Nigeria violence, says bandit leader
nigeria.description: Decades of discrimination and extortion against Fulani herders are stoking the growing violence in northern Nigeria — unrest which will only swell until authorities tame the rampant corruption in the region, a bandit kingpin told AFP in a rare interview. Northwest and central Nigeria have for years been terrorised by gangs known locally as “bandits”, who raid villages, rustle cattle, conduct kidnappings and impose “taxes” on farmers and miners. The interview with one such gang leader came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, in a piece published Thursday, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and AFP northern Nigeria reporter Aminu Abubakar. “Years of injustices are what pushed Fulani herders into banditry. We were never criminals before,” a bandit leader named Babangida said. Banditry traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders. The conflict has spiralled from raids and revenge attacks into broader, complex criminality by gangs numbering from around a dozen to well into the hundreds. They have created a kidnapping economy that raises hundreds of thousands of dollars, and at times entered alliances with Nigerian jihadists. After months of negotiation, Babangida agreed to an interview in a remote Katsina state village, following the intervention of a former government peace negotiator. “Justice is the only way out. When justice is upheld, everyone will live in peace,” said the bandit, who asked only to be identified by his first name. In the meantime, violence reigns: last week, in neighbouring Zamfara state, bandits set fire to a home during a raid, killing a family of 12. Earlier this month, gunmen killed eight police officers, and in September, more than 80 people, mostly women, were kidnapped in Zamfara and Niger states — many while working their fields. Worsening insecurity has become a major issue in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. – Corruption – Clad in a blue kaftan, the 38-year-old passes for a normal villager, save for the Kalashnikov rifle in his hand. “No bandit just picked up a gun overnight and turned to violence. There is always a story behind it,” said Babangida, sheltering from the scorching heat under a neem tree. Babangida said he turned to banditry a decade ago after his family’s 97 cows were seized by a team of police and vigilantes. He described the raid as based on indiscriminate suspicions that all Fulani are bandits. He was forced to pay millions of naira (thousands of dollars) to post bail for his mother and brother. nigeria.title: INEC warns Okada riders against political violence in Oyo
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators in Oyo State against allowing politicians to use them as instruments of violence, thuggery and electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission urged members of transport unions to resist attempts to involve them in activities capable of undermining public peace and the credibility of the electoral process before, during and after the elections. The Oyo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Adeniran Tella, gave the warning on Thursday at the 2026 Day celebration of the Amalgamated Commercial Tricycle and Motorcycle Owners, Repairs and Riders Association of Nigeria (ACOMORAN), held alongside the launch of a book authored by the union’s chairman, Solomon Olugbode, at the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium, Oke-Ado, Ibadan. Tella, who was represented by the Head of INEC’s Information Unit, Olayiwola Awolowo, also urged members of the association to encourage their passengers and other members of the public to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). He stressed the importance of civic participation in the electoral process, saying commercial transport operators had a responsibility to protect democracy rather than allow themselves to be recruited into activities capable of threatening national security. “Let me be clear, do not allow yourselves to be used as instruments of violence or thuggery. The Nigeria Police Force has warned that the law will take its full course against anyone, no matter their status, who threatens public peace or engages in criminal conduct before, during or after the elections,” he said. Specifically, he charged ACOMORAN members to shun political violence, warning them against transporting weapons, money for vote-buying or individuals intending to disrupt the elections. “Your motorcycle or tricycle is a tool of livelihood, not a weapon of destruction. I urge you to remain politically neutral as a union,” he added. The INEC representative also cautioned the association against allowing its structures and operational resources to be deployed in support of any political party, noting that members retained the right to support candidates of their choice in their individual capacities. “While you have the right to support any candidate of your choice as individuals, the union’s infrastructure must never be hijacked to favour one party over another,” he said. He urged the transport operators to support INEC’s election logistics by ensuring the timely and safe movement of electoral materials and personnel whenever engaged by the commission. He also called on members to serve as voter education ambassadors by promoting peace, tolerance and responsible voting at motor parks and among their passengers. nigeria.title: Protesters block INEC chair’s vehicle in London, demand resignation
nigeria.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, was confronted by protesters in London on Thursday over alleged irregularities in the preliminary voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The demonstrators surrounded the vehicle conveying Amupitan outside Chatham House, where he was expected to participate in a panel discussion on Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 polls. The protesters, believed to be Nigerians living abroad, shouted insults at the INEC chairman and accused the commission of abandoning its neutrality in favour of President Bola Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress. They also demanded Amupitan’s resignation, labelling INEC a “criminal organisation” over alleged duplicate voter registrations, questionable polling units and photographs suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence. The demonstration followed mounting criticism of the commission after images and records purportedly showing suspicious entries in the preliminary voters’ register circulated publicly. INEC had acknowledged irregularities in the registration process and announced an investigation into the affected records, further fuelling the controversy. ‘Trust me I won’t fail you’ Speaking earlier at the event, Amupitan asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch. nigeria.title: Anambra requires 1,000 megawatts of electricity to power its growing economy – Soludo
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo has said that the state requires about 1,000 megawatts of electricity to adequately power its growing economy. Delivering the keynote address at the Electricity Market Investment Roundtable organised by the Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission (ASERC) in Awka, the governor lamented that Anambra currently receives only about 120 megawatts, describing the huge gap as both a major challenge and an investment opportunity. “Without electricity, there will be no manufacturing. Without energy, only little can happen. For us, it is very consequential. We are here to do business. Anambra is ready for business,” the governor declared. Soludo urged investors to take advantage of the numerous opportunities in the state’s electricity market, particularly those connected with the state’s proposed Mixed Industrial City and aerotropolis. The governor threw open the state’s electricity market to investors, declaring that Anambra is ready for business as it seeks to bridge a massive power deficit threatening its industrial and economic growth. To the participants at the summit, Soludo added: “Tell us when, where and how we can get the 1,000 megawatts. Let’s get the plan, a clear roadmap, actionable, verifiable roadmap. Anambra is a land of opportunities. This is a summit for closing deals. Let’s get it done. “Move beyond discussions and produce a practical, measurable and verifiable roadmap for closing the state’s electricity gap.” The governor reiterated his administration’s determination to create an enabling environment for private-sector participation in the electricity market. Chairman of Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission, ASERC, Professor Frank Okafor, commended the governor for driving innovation and reforms in the state’s energy sector. He acknowledged the substantial electricity deficit in Anambra, explaining that the roundtable was convened to bring stakeholders together to develop practical solutions to the challenge. “We are here to think together and come up with a solution that will help to overcome the challenge,” Okafor said. Former chairman of the Nigeria Communications Commission, NCC, Engr. Ernest Ndukwe, who chaired the event, noted that Governor Soludo has the capacity to deliver the changes required in the state’s electricity sector. nigeria.title: Swiss woman evacuated from Nigeria over Ebola discharged in Geneva
nigeria.description: A Swiss woman who contracted the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola linked to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has been discharged from hospital in Geneva, Switzerland. The woman, who is the wife of a Swiss embassy employee in Abuja, was evacuated from Nigeria alongside her husband on October 26 after contracting the virus. Benoit Carpentier, spokesperson for the University Hospitals of Geneva (HUG), said the patient received supportive medical care, including hydration and management of potential complications associated with the disease. “The patient has recovered. She was discharged from hospital yesterday (Wednesday),” he told AFP, confirming a report by Tribune de Genève. The woman’s husband reportedly showed no symptoms of the disease, while his quarantine was lifted on November 4. Nigeria announced the Ebola case on October 20, confirming that it involved the Bundibugyo strain, the same variant responsible for the latest outbreak in the DRC. The strain remains a major public health concern as there is currently no specific approved treatment or vaccine against it. The outbreak was officially detected in the DRC in May and has since infected more than 11,000 people, with over 5,400 deaths recorded. Cases have also been detected in Uganda and Kenya, raising concerns about the spread of the disease across the region. nigeria.title: Nigeria taking religious violence more seriously after US CPC listing – Officials
nigeria.description: US State Department officials have said Nigeria is taking religious violence more seriously following its designation as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC) by President Donald Trump, but warned that more concrete action is needed to protect vulnerable communities and bring perpetrators to justice. The officials made the assessment on Thursday during a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s response to attacks on vulnerable communities since the US placed the country on its CPC list. President Trump redesignated Nigeria as a CPC over allegations of Christian persecution and genocide before the US military launched a missile strike against terrorist targets in Sokoto State on Christmas Day. Nigeria and the US have since entered into a military partnership targeting terrorists in the country’s northern region and established a joint working group to address Washington’s concerns over religious violence. The hearing was convened by Chris Smith, Chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Africa Subcommittee, to examine Nigeria’s response to attacks on vulnerable communities following the CPC designation. Speaking at the hearing, Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, said the State Department had intensified engagements with Nigerian officials to address attacks against Christian communities and ensure accountability for perpetrators. He, however, acknowledged that the violence had persisted, stressing that Washington expected measurable improvements in security deployments, early responses to warnings of impending attacks and prosecution of those responsible. “We are expecting results — protection for Christian communities in the Middle Belt through increased Nigerian security and law enforcement deployments, more timely and effective responses to early warnings of impending attacks, accountability for perpetrators through stronger courts and security services, and deeper military-to-military cooperation,” he said. Garcia said the US was pursuing a coordinated approach to strengthening Nigeria’s security architecture through capacity building, expanded use of biometric data to identify perpetrators and financial action plans to disrupt terrorist financing networks. “Though Nigeria has reported progress, under Secretary Hooker made it clear in the joint working group second session that this pace is insufficient,” he added. Also speaking, Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour, said the US had continued to urge the Nigerian government to repeal blasphemy laws or, at the minimum, stop enforcing them. Barnes said Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a CPC had prompted the country to take religious violence and related concerns more seriously. “The government has reported leadership changes, strategically deployed military forces, and increased arrests and prosecutions,” he said. nigeria.title: Fasoranti’s death ends an era, says Akure communities
nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Akure Speaking Communities Development Initiative (ASCDI) has described the death of Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, as the end of an era of wisdom, exemplary leadership, patriotism and selfless service to Akureland, Yorubaland and Nigeria. The group said the late elder statesman was a moral compass whose life and leadership inspired generations, describing his death as a profound loss to the people of Akure, the Yoruba nation and the country. In a condolence statement issued in Akure and signed by its Chairman, Air Commodore Adewale Ogunmodede (retd.), and Secretary, Dr Olawale Ademola, ASCDI said it received the news of his passing with profound sorrow. It described Fasoranti as an illustrious son of Akureland, a respected statesman and a distinguished Yoruba leader. “Pa Fasoranti was not merely an elder statesman; he was a moral compass, a symbol of courage, an embodiment of integrity, and a custodian of the cherished values and traditions of our people. “His life represented the finest ideals of community service, peaceful coexistence, justice, unity, and the pursuit of collective progress,” the statement said. The organisation noted that as leader of Afenifere and a prominent voice in national affairs, Fasoranti devoted much of his life to championing the interests of the Yoruba people, promoting democratic ideals and advocating fairness, equity and good governance in Nigeria. For the Akure Speaking Communities across Ifedore, Akure North and Akure South Local Government Areas of Ondo State, ASCDI said his death represented an immeasurable loss. It described him as a towering figure whose wisdom, experience and fatherly guidance inspired generations of leaders and community development advocates. “His enduring legacy reminds us that true greatness is measured not by personal accomplishments alone, but by the positive impact one makes on society and the values one leaves behind for succeeding generations,” it added. The group urged sons and daughters of Akure Speaking Communities, both at home and in the diaspora, to honour his memory by strengthening their commitment to unity, peaceful coexistence, cultural preservation and sustainable community development. It also extended its condolences to the Fasoranti family, the Deji and other royal fathers in the Akure Speaking Communities, the leadership and members of Afenifere, the Ondo State Government and people, as well as the Yoruba nation. “We pray that Almighty God grants the bereaved family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss and grants the departed patriarch eternal rest. “Although Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti may have departed this earthly realm, his ideals, sacrifices, wisdom, and contributions to humanity will remain indelibly engraved in the annals of our history,” the statement said. nigeria.description: By Emmma Nnadozie A 24-year-old student of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, has recounted how he narrowly escaped death during an off-campus party that claimed the lives of four students in Nsukka, Enugu State. The survivor, an Art Education student, said he lost consciousness after one of the participants vomited during the party, only to regain consciousness several hours later and discover his friends lying motionless on the floor. Recounting his experience with our Crime Editor, the student said the gathering was organised by his friend, David, to celebrate the completion of his final examinations. According to him, the host bought two bottles of alcoholic drinks, Magic Moment and Best, which they took to his residence at Hilltop, Nsukka, where about 10 people gathered for the celebration. He said the party started around 11:30 a.m., adding that the participants shared the drinks while engaging in a Truth and Dare game for entertainment. He narrated: “During the party, one of the participants started vomiting. I took him to the toilet and asked him to clean himself up. I then came out to clean the vomit on the floor. “After that, I suddenly lost consciousness. However, I noticed that my legs had become stiff, and I could no longer walk. “When I regained consciousness at about 9 p.m., I heard someone saying that a ghost was shaking. I woke up and managed to look into the parlour, where I saw the host and other participants lying on the floor.” The survivor said he immediately contacted a friend, who came to the house, saw their condition and left. He expressed disappointment that another person who reportedly arrived at the scene started recording them instead of making efforts to rescue them. He said he subsequently contacted another friend, who came and helped convey them to Bishop Shanahan Hospital and other hospitals in Nsukka for medical attention. Explaining the circumstances surrounding the gathering, the survivor said the participants were inside the parlour with the doors and windows shut, while a generator was operating outside in the corridor. nigeria.title: Regulators, private sector leaders, others to review local content growth
nigeria.description: Regulatory authorities, private sector leaders and legislators have concluded arrangement for a closed-door Local Content Roundtable to review Nigeria’s journey path of localizing its industries over the years. The engagement, driven by the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum 2026, is designed to shift the national conversation from indigenous participation to sustainable, in-country capacity development. It would also focus around the team: ‘‘Building Sustainable Local Capacity: Scaling Capability, Enabling Ownership and Funding Growth’’, and will confront the issue of physical, technological or intellectual capacity created in Nigeria since the inception of the policy in 2010. “Every year at PNC, we celebrate the percentage. This year, we wanted a room that explores what that percentage is made of, and how we build on it,” said Wemimo Oyelana, Portfolio and Country Director, dmg events, organizers of the meeting. He stated further: “The skills, technology and industrial capacity developed through projects over the past 16 years are real assets. The Roundtable will bring stakeholders together to define what lasting Nigerian capacity looks like, how it can be measured, and how we grow it at scale.” According to the organizers, PNC 2026 will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, investors and indigenous businesses to address the priorities shaping the next phase of Nigerian Content development. For operators and project developers, the discussions will examine how local capacity can support project delivery and long-term competitiveness. nigeria.title: My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain
nigeria.description: Flamingos captain, Harmony Chidi, has revealed how her mother initially opposed her ambition to become a professional footballer and wanted her to get married following the early death of her father. The 17-year-old, who led Nigeria to a historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, said her grandmother and foster father played crucial roles in keeping her football dream alive despite the opposition. Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to become the first African country to win the competition. Speaking in an interview with BBC Pidgin, Chidi said her mother was initially unwilling to allow her to pursue football after the death of her father, but her grandmother stood by her and encouraged her to continue. “When I started football, my mother didn’t want me to play. My father died early, so my mother wanted me to get married. It was my grandmother who stood by me and pushed me to play football. Unfortunately, my grandmother is late,” she said. The Bayelsa Queens striker also credited her foster father, Prince Chidi, owner of her grassroots team, Imo Strikers, for providing the encouragement and support she needed to pursue her ambition. “It wasn’t easy until I met my foster father, Prince Chidi. He is the owner of my grassroots team, Imo Strikers, and he encourages me, making sure that I achieve my dream,” she added. Chidi also recounted how a career-threatening injury nearly ended her football ambition and prevented her from featuring at the previous edition of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. She described the injury as the most difficult period of her career, saying the experience was made worse by the withdrawal of friends who had previously been around her. “There is nothing that has been more difficult than my injury. It is an injury that has killed the dream of many players in Nigeria. All my friends deserted me and it was tough. I even thought of an alternative plan,” she recounted. However, the teenager overcame the setback, returned to action and eventually captained Nigeria to its historic world title in Morocco. Despite the milestone achievement, Chidi said she was determined to reach greater heights, naming Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Nigerian women’s football star Asisat Oshoala as players she admired and hoped to surpass. “I have like five players that I want to be like: Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Asisat Oshoala. nigeria.title: Elumelu backs Nigeria’s N52,500 pension floor, praises
nigeria.description: industry-funded retiree healthcare Chairman of Heirs Holdings and Transcorp, Mr. Tony Elumelu, has said that the PenCare Retiree Healthcare Initiative and the National Minimum Pension Guarantee will address two fundamental concerns of every retiree: access to healthcare and security of income. Elumelu who stated this while giving his remarks at the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives Launch in Abuja noted that the private sector stands ready to support policies and partnerships that strengthen our institutions. It will be recalled that Nigeria has started paying a guaranteed minimum pension of N52,500 a month to retirees in the Contributory Pension Scheme, the system of individual retirement accounts for workers. The provision has been in the country’s pension law since 2004 but was never used. President Bola Tinubu also launched PenCare, a free healthcare plan for low-income retirees that the pension industry pays for. Elumelu called the two programmes “investments in human dignity.” The Minimum Pension Guarantee takes effect immediately and will be run by the National Pension Commission (PenCom). He particularly praised the pension industry for funding PenCare, calling it “a powerful demonstration of what responsible institutions can achieve when they put people first.” PenCom Director-General, Omolola Oloworaran said 173,209 retirees currently receive less than N52,500 and will be raised to that level. Some had been receiving just over N20,000 a month. The guarantee is paid from a N400 billion Pension Protection Fund, to which the federal government and the pension industry have contributed. State governments must also pay in before their retirees can benefit. “If people are not contributing, we’ll run out of funds,” Oloworaran said. She said the N52,500 figure “was not plucked from the air. nigeria.title: Amupitan denies owning pro-APC X account
nigeria.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has denied owning or operating an X account allegedly used to express support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) during the 2023 general election. Amupitan said the controversy had been referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the office of the Inspector-General of Police, adding that an independent investigative report had also been obtained. He spoke on Thursday during a dialogue at Chatham House in London, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative, with the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Responding to a question on whether an independent investigation had established that he was not behind the disputed account, the INEC chairman said the matter had been reported to the relevant security agencies. “We have an independent report and the matter was also reported to the DSS as well as to the IG,” he said. Amupitan maintained that he had never operated an X account, explaining that his attempt to contact the social media platform to address the allegation was unsuccessful because he was not a registered user. “I never had an X account. I tried to get in touch with X, but there’s no way if you don’t have an account,” he said. He further disclosed that some civil society organisations had expressed interest in investigating the controversy. Insisting that he had never operated the disputed account, Amupitan said his regular email platform was Yahoo. “I have my Yahoo mail. I check Yahoo mail. It was never my account. And that is the truth,” he said. The INEC chairman also suggested that the timing of the controversy was part of an attempt to discredit him and undermine the electoral commission, linking its emergence to a court ruling concerning the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the interpretation of the status quo ante bellum order. “Remember the background. That issue came up when the court ruled that ADC had an issue, and the concept of status quo ante bellum. I don’t want to go back into it. But at the same time, it came about that time,” he said. He added that attempts to discredit the commission could be channelled through attacks on its leadership. “The only way that people could bring down an institution was to say, ‘Oh, this person,’” he said. nigeria.title: Doherty warns against underestimating Obi’s influence after attack on NDC supporters
nigeria.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, has warned politicians against underestimating Peter Obi’s political influence, saying the former Anambra State governor still commands a strong support base despite his defection from the Labour Party. Doherty said the resistance by NDC supporters to an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday showed that the enthusiasm which defined Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign remained strong. He spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today following the disruption of the meeting at Classic Event Place, Oregun, Ikeja. Dismissing suggestions that Obi’s defection to the NDC could weaken his political appeal, Doherty argued that his popularity was rooted in his political philosophy rather than the party under which he contests elections. “The reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. He cautioned those seeking to downplay Obi’s political relevance, describing such a position as a grave mistake. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. Doherty said the reaction of supporters to the attack was evidence that Obi’s political movement had not lost the energy it demonstrated during the 2023 election. He said the attackers might have expected supporters to abandon the venue in fear, but were instead confronted by people determined to defend their rights. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind,” he said. He described the attack as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary” and praised supporters who resisted the assailants, calling them heroes. Suspected political thugs reportedly invaded the venue ahead of Obi’s arrival, allegedly armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones. They vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. The confrontation disrupted activities before security operatives intervened. The meeting later proceeded, with Obi, Senator Victor Umeh, activist Aisha Yesufu and other party figures in attendance. nigeria.title: INEC to obey court on Atiku’s ADC candidacy – Amupitan
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said it will abide by the final court decision on former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s eligibility to contest the 2027 presidential election on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, said the commission was constitutionally obligated to comply with court orders, particularly decisions of the Supreme Court, irrespective of their political implications. Amupitan spoke on Thursday during a dialogue at Chatham House in London, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative, with the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Responding to a question on whether Atiku could contest on the ADC platform if the judgment nullifying the leadership of the faction led by former Senate President, David Mark, was upheld, Amupitan said INEC would be guided by the outcome of the legal process. “If he eventually fails, well, I’m obligated under Section 285 of the Constitution of Nigeria to obey every court order, especially if it is from the Supreme Court,” he said. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had advocated an accelerated hearing of the ADC leadership dispute when it emerged in April, insisting that the matter should be resolved within three weeks to avoid complications for the 2027 electoral process. “When it happened in April, the position of the commission was that the matter should be resolved within three weeks,” he said. He explained that INEC had complied with a court directive to suspend action and await the determination of the dispute, which subsequently proceeded on appeal. Amupitan also expressed concern over the growing number of election-related cases involving the commission, disclosing that INEC had more than 300 pending court cases with the 2027 elections about 66 days away. “Some of those issues we have with court cases, over 300 cases hanging on the neck of INEC, and elections is just about 66 days away,” he said. He disclosed that INEC had commenced procurement of sensitive materials for the 2027 elections, stressing the need for reforms to ensure that pre-election disputes were resolved between six months and one year before polling. According to him, early resolution of such disputes would allow the commission sufficient time to complete its logistical and operational preparations for elections. The INEC chairman further acknowledged that the commission often faced public criticism when implementing judicial decisions but maintained that it was bound by the law. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion The DOJ said Thursday it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, part of a freeze of more than $2.7 billion that officials said halted about half of North Korea’s October exchange heist. In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack. Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.” The freeze of more than $2.7 billion is a joint figure for U.S. government and private-sector efforts. Of that amount, the DOJ said it has already obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion. The underlying court papers were not posted with the announcement. The $1.2 billion is not newly recovered money but comes out of the roughly $2.85 billion Binance said on Nov. 3 had been frozen or intercepted, and Thursday’s court authorization is the legal step that lets the government move toward taking ownership of those funds through forfeiture, where until now they had simply been frozen at the token issuers. Even that freeze is not the end of the trail. The DOJ said TraderTraitor actors are still moving the stolen assets through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges, and that tracing, seizure and forfeiture work continues. Last week, on Oct. 31, the FBI, with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to North Korea and urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses the actors are using. The alert said investigators have seen the stolen assets converted primarily into ether. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms. Neither the Justice Department nor Europol split the $234 million between cash and cryptocurrency, and neither named bitcoin or any other coin in the official totals. Europol put the European share at more than €60 million in cash and cryptocurrencies, alongside 950 kilograms of drugs and 57 firearms, and the U.S. share at more than €150 million, or $166 million, in cash and cryptocurrencies, plus more than 4.8 metric tons of drugs and 152 firearms. Those regional money figures still combine cash and crypto. Europol said its forensic and blockchain analysis teams traced illicit transactions as part of the work. Individual cases point to Monero and bitcoin The closest official window into how the vendors were paid comes from the cases the Justice Department highlighted and from court papers posted with the announcement. Alexander Green, 32, of Jacksonville, North Carolina, was arrested in June and charged in the Southern District of Ohio with conspiracy to distribute controlled substances, including fentanyl. The department said he allegedly operated a vendor called STARLABS on DrugHub, which it described as a Monero-only dark web market, and that the group has been linked to two overdose deaths. A criminal complaint says undercover purchases from STARLABS were made “in exchange for cryptocurrency.” If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in prison. In a separate Florida arrest, brothers Stanislav Chernyshov, 30, and Vladislav Chernyshov, 35, are charged in the Eastern District of Virginia with conspiracy to distribute Schedule I synthetic opioids. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is not a trend that can be reversed. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. entertainment.title: Olumide Oworu Declares House of Representatives Bid for Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027

He will be running under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). Olumide, who grew up in Surulere, Lagos, has a long-standing connection to the constituency. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he wrote. Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.” His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. The 25-year-old will receive the honour at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 30 November. Born in a refugee camp in Ethiopia and raised in Canada, Awar’s journey to the international fashion scene has taken her from being discovered in Alberta to walking some of the world’s biggest runways. sports.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
sports.description: Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday [Getty Images] As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," one woman watching the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news [BBC] Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. There's a sense of injustice that Australia can't escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story [Getty Images] Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. David Warner, who received the most severe punishment of the Cape Town trio, said Khawaja was telling the truth and that Cummins' press conference denying the claims "threw him under the bus". Steve

Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said.
