sports.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
sports.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. sports.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
sports.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. sports.title: Bills vs Jets prediction and key matchups for tricky division game
sports.description: ORCHARD PARK - If there was a moment when the team-wide frustration that the New York Jets have experienced this season boiled to a head, it was last Sunday in Kansas City when quarterback Geno Smith momentarily lost his mind. In the second quarter of what became their fourth straight loss, the Jets were leading 9-7 when Braelon Allen lost a fumble that was recovered by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman. As Gilman began his return, Smith rushed over and launched himself with intent and knocked Gilman flat at the Jets 24, a stunning display of physicality from a quarterback. “It's something that you really don't want to happen, but competitors are going to compete, so I'm not surprised that it happened, but that's something that you don't want from your starting quarterback,” coach Aaron Glenn said. Smith knew the fumble was a huge mistake and sure enough, the Chiefs scored two plays later and grabbed a lead they never relinquished in their 35-12 blowout. Later in the game, following another failed Jets possession, Smith came to the sideline and slammed his helmet to the ground, the inevitability of falling to 2-7 clearly getting to him. As usual in mid-November, the Jets are already in playing-out-the-string mode, but they have a great chance to make a statement Sunday when they host the 7-1 Buffalo Bills . There isn’t too much left to play for downstate, but beating the AFC’s No. 1 team and damaging the Bills’ quest for the No. 1 seed would certainly provide some professional joy, especially considering the two 30-10 and 35-8 beatings Buffalo put on New York last year. “We're not going to hide from the fact that we're 2-7,” said Glenn, who is likely coaching for his job so every possible victory is crucial. “We own that, but man, we're still working our (butts) off to make sure we fix that. We like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that. When you look at the seven losses, and this is just the facts, five of the teams were playoff-caliber teams. I think five of them were one-score games. There's a number of things that we got to fix and get better at, but we feel like, man, we're right on the cusp of trying to break through.” Joe Brady claims he never pays attention to the standings or an opponent’s record, but he knows the Jets are 2-7, and he also knows that a few plays here or there could have altered the course of their season. Although the 22-year-old Spain international has struggled for regular starts this season, he remains determined to stay at Camp Nou and win back his place in the starting line-up. Midfielder rules out Camp Nou exit Reports from Marca reveal that the idea of departing Catalonia has never "crossed the player's mind", while sporting director Deco has zero desire to sanction a sale. Both the 22-year-old's camp and club hierarchy insist his future is completely secure despite recent enquiries from Italy and Germany. Having made 175 senior appearances since joining La Masia from Real Betis in 2015, the academy graduate wants to stay put. Fierce competition limits starting opportunities Gavi has been restricted to just 229 minutes across nine appearances this term - comprising five La Liga outings and four in the Champions League - with only two of those coming as a starter. Head coach Hansi Flick currently favours a first-choice double pivot of Pedri and Rodri, while youngster Marc Bernal has served as the primary deputy whenever either is unavailable, including during last weekend's victory away at Atletico Madrid. Pathways further forward are similarly congested for the versatile Andalusian. Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo currently share the attacking midfield duties, while Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi rotate on the left flank. Strong bond underpins mutual confidence Even though the Spanish publication notes that the midfielder is "not happy with his role", his motivation remains high and he stays "confident" of earning more minutes as the campaign progresses. His limited involvement has not affected his "close relationship" with Flick, who admires the player's relentless character and footballing ability. Gavi even views the German tactician as a father figure, a bond highlighted when the pair shared a warm embrace on the touchline after sealing victory at the Metropolitano last weekend . Demanding winter schedule promises rotation With Barcelona facing a packed and demanding fixture list after the November international break, Flick is expected to rotate his squad far more frequently over the coming months. technology.description: The next version of the C++ programming language may be delayed at the last minute due to a dispute over a security-enhancing Contracts feature. Contracts have deeply split C++ technical maintainers. One group backs the C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup , who is against the technology in its present form in grounds it was hastily implemented. But others are eager to see Contracts implemented, even arguing the tech's detractors are poisoning the C++ development process itself. The disagreement boiled over just before a vote to ratify the new version of the language. In October, the Draft International Standard (DIS) of C++26 failed its ISO ballot — the next-to-last stage in the International Organization for Standardization’s approval process during which a standard's technical details are formally ratified by a set of national standards bodies. The ballot saw 13 votes cast in favor, 9 against, and 12 abstentions, failing to meet the ISO requirement of having no more than 25 percent negative votes. Contracts was the major sticking point for those voting nay. Contracts dispute Contracts allow developers to add preconditions and postconditions to code, as well as assertions that check whether specified conditions hold. Such checks can help catch programming errors that might otherwise lead to undefined behavior. Design by Contract has long been a feature of languages like Ada and Eiffel . Developers have proposed adding Contracts to C++ for at least a decade, after when they were abruptly yanked from C++20 owing to concerns over dangerous defaults. But Stroustrup roasted the revised proposal ( P2900 ) that made it into C++26. “The P2900 contracts and extensions aim to change the nature of C++ and are an existential threat to C++, adding complexity and bloat,” Stroustrup and his colleagues wrote in a paper last August. They noted that the implementation is messy, outdated, not sufficiently tested , and could be more effectively implemented as a library. Not everyone agrees. technology.title: Developer cleverly shrank 2,600 lines of C into a six-line script but still ending up losing sleep
technology.description: Working in tech support can be thankless when gormless colleagues leave you sleepless. Which is why, each Friday, The Register runs a new instalment of On Call – the reader contributed column which ensures your work to keep tech alive doesn't remain unnoticed. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Tim" who told that while working for a phone company he once rewrote 2,650 lines of C as a six line shell script. He performed that feat after being asked to fix a data transfer program that, strangely, included a bespoke implementation of the venerable File Transfer Protocol (FTP). "Writing the script took eight hours, most of it tracking down the source code of FTP so I could see if it would do what I wanted," Tim wrote. This story took place before the World Wide Web became the way to find information online. To find the code he needed, Tim therefore used a Wide Area Information Server (WAIS) to search remote databases. "In those days, there was no Linux and AT&T had licensed the Unix source code to universities with the struct proviso that it never be made publicly available," Tim explained. "It took me quite some time using WAIS to track it down – the security could have been better – and read the code." Having found what he needed, Tim wrote his script, which ran overnight to collect data from the telco's switches, tidied up the raw info, and uploaded it to a mainframe. "It would automatically page me if it couldn't connect to a switch or mainframe after three attempts," he explained. The script worked fine, but the telco's networks didn't. Tim's pager was soon going off two or three times a night, every night. After two weeks of interrupted sleep, Tim's manager kindly told him to give the pager to a colleague. But that colleague habitually left the pager at work, forgot to turn it on, or conveniently placed it out of earshot. So Tim reluctantly took back the pager and endured another few weeks of nightly interruptions. How many consecutive sleepless nights have you endured while On Call? If you have enough energy, click here to send your story with On Call so we can share it on a future Friday. ®

technology.title: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 re-educated with a more Western worldview
technology.description: An American AI lab has re-educated Qwen3.8-27B, a popular open-weight large language model from Alibaba, so the software forgets its Chinese ancestry. Nous Research, an Austin, Texas-based AI lab, has subjected the model to re-education through training, not to be confused with China's " Re-education Through Labor " system. With the help of a post-training process, Qwen3.8-27B has been reborn under the name Arete "to reinforce Western values on a Chinese-trained model." What qualifies as a "Western value" remains open to interpretation. "Open-weight Chinese models are among the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior baked into the weights," Nous Research wrote in a blog post . Your correspondent tested this with a variant model, Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-6bit, locally. Asked about events during 1989 in Tiananmen Square, the model either refused to discuss the topic or provided euphemistic response. What's perhaps more surprising is that Anthropic claims operators affiliated with Alibaba's Qwen lab used outputs from its Claude models to train competing AI models via distillation . Nous Research, maker of the Hermes Agent , cites that sort of censorship as a risk for users of AI models trained in China. The concern comes amid broader scrutiny of Chinese influence in the tech industry, heightened by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation following controversy involving a woman US intelligence has accused of spying for China. Nous says the risk posed by Chinese-made AI models go beyond promoting Beijing's worldview. Some Middle Kingdom models have been found to produce more vulnerable code under certain conditions, according to a study by Booz Allen Hamilton, which does a lot of business with the US government. Hirundo, a vendor which says it is building "the first Machine Unlearning Platform to ensure that AI models only know what they should," makes the same argument . The company also notes that its efforts to apply "unlearning" to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B saw a dramatic drop in output that reflects Communist Party of China's preferred censorship, propaganda messaging, or bias. 89.8 percent of the model's output reflected those values before unlearning reduced the incidence to 2.8 percent. Nous Research did not achieve such dramatic results, but did see an overall reduction in viewpoints deemed to be propaganda. "On our evaluation, Arete-27B raised its fact score from 2.32 to 2.98 out of 5 and cut answers containing propaganda from 22 percent to 1 percent, in line with the Western models we tested," the company said. The court also allowed the takedown of cloud-based infrastructure used in a Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) social engineering scheme called “FaceStealer” that has amassed more than $400 million in the last 18 months. It’s called FaceStealer because it involved secretly recorded webcam videos. Victims are typically people working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, along with open source software developers and maintainers who DPRK hackers target in the hope of accessing the software repositories they control as the first step towards creating supply chain attacks. 900+ faces stolen The FBI said it had seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to these tech workers. Here’s how the attack works. First, the North Koreans send targets an invitation to join a video meeting. Those invitations come from hijacked accounts that the next intended victim may find familiar or credible. “You're going to think it's real because it's going to be based on either conversations or interests you've expressed in the past with this actual person,” said special agent Jeremy Robertson, who oversees counterintelligence and cyber investigations at FBI Los Angeles. “They're going to then send you a link to catch up, and it's usually a calendar invite, and it's going to have some typo-squatted URLs in there,” he told reporters on Thursday. The URL directs the victim to a fake Zoom or Teams meeting, and the cybercriminals record the target’s webcam video while playing a phony, prerecorded video of the person who purportedly sent the meeting invite. Sometimes the hackers also use deepfake videos of well-known individuals in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, we’re told. “When you log in, whoever invited you – your friend or business associate – is going to be on the screen, but you're not going to hear any audio,” Robertson said. “But you're going to see their face, you're going to see them looking around, you're going to see them mouthing some words, and then in the text box you're going to receive some instructions.” ‘You’re on mute’ as a social engineering vector The text box tells the victim that the person on the other end of the video call can’t hear them, they need to upgrade their software for the audio to work properly, and it sends a link to the supposed fix. technology.title: Microsoft struggling to fix massive cloud outage that's taken down email and Intune
technology.description: Microsoft is struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became “overwhelmed” and its attempts to fix the problem failed. The incident started at around 18:00 UTC on November 12, and meant services including Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot 365, and Defender for Office 365 became unavailable. Admins trying to figure out what was wrong couldn’t access tools like Intune or the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center – they went down, too. On its X feed, Microsoft blamed “a problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.” The company said it hasn’t spotted any changes to its systems that might have sparked the incident, but its early investigation “indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health.” The company’s status page offers contradictory information, saying Microsoft’s people are “assessing whether reverting the small number of recent configuration updates we identified could help accelerate recovery.” According to a Xeet published at around 22:00 UTC, Microsoft said it found and validated an alternative service health check method, “which allowed a subset of affected servers to successfully return to service.” “We're continuing to work through restarting and validating the affected servers to safely return them to service, and we're exploring opportunities to expedite this process,” the company wrote. But those efforts may not be working. “We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the status page advises. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.” The incident means email is not flowing for many Microsoft customers: friends and family of Reg writers tell us their working days are severely disrupted. Microsoft’s most recent Xeet on the matter, published about an hour before this story went live, says it's trying to validate a potential recovery by “isolating a portion of infrastructure, restarting affected components, and reintroducing traffic to confirm the services remain stable before applying the change more broadly.” But the software giant hasn’t offered any timeline for full service restoration. This is a developing situation and The Reg will update this story as more information becomes available. ® UPDATED AT 00:35 UTC November 13 to add news that Microsoft says it has brought some servers back online and that they " initially remain healthy" but "can become unresponsive again once they begin receiving traffic." So not usefully healthy at all, then. "We're analyzing diagnostic data from these servers with our networking and platform experts to determine what's triggering this behavior," the company advised.

The company's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms. On Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. And Ship 42 itself is connected to the beloved book, by virtue of its serial number. In "The Hitchhiker's Guide," a supercomputer named Deep Mind is asked to come up with "the answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything." It thinks for 7.5 million years and comes up with "42." SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has voiced his affection for "The Hitchhiker's Guide" in the past — and he has already paid tribute to it with a well-placed "Don't panic." The debut launch of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket back in February 2018 sent Musk's red Tesla Roadster into orbit around the sun , with a spacesuit-clad mannequin named Starman at the wheel and its entertainment display programmed to read "Don't panic!" science.title: Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today (Nov. 13)
science.description: null SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live. Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before. You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan. Composite photo showing the Super Heavy booster of SpaceX's Starship megarocket coming in for a landing on the launch mount on Oct. 13, 2024. (Image credit: SpaceX via X) Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight. The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the company has said. SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy , pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover. So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description . The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit . The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28. Ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff. There's no guarantee things will go according to plan, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile. So it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page .

NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison. Scientists began using satellites to map mangrove forests in the 1970s after the launch of the first Landsat satellite. For decades, the story they told about mangroves was dominated by loss and decline. Research published in Science suggests that the tide has turned. A global rebound began around 2010, the scientists found, led by the expansion of mangrove forests in Asia, Australia, and South America. The researchers analyzed Landsat imagery collected between 1984 and 2023, looking for signs of changes in the extent and density of mangrove canopy. They tallied losses of nearly 3,000 square kilometers (1,200 square miles) between 1984 and 2010, followed by an unexpected increase of nearly 2,000 square kilometers (770 square miles) of mangroves after 2010. They also found that many of today’s mangrove forests have denser, more closed canopies than they did in 2010, a sign of healthier, less degraded forests, particularly in South America. “Other research groups have mapped and analyzed long-term changes in select regions, but these are the first global mangrove maps that cover such a long period,” said Zhen Zhang, an environmental scientist at Tulane University. “About two-thirds of the expansion was due to mangroves colonizing new areas and the other third due to restoration and regrowth in degraded areas,” he added. One of the most notable reversals occurred in Southeast Asia—especially Burma (Myanmar). The country lost mangroves rapidly in the 1980s and 1990s due to the expansion of agriculture, aquaculture, and firewood harvesting in coastal areas, but the trend reversed around 2010, when mangrove area began expanding in many places. The authors attribute the turnaround to increased awareness and restoration efforts after the devastating Indian Ocean tsunami in 2004 , strengthened legal protections for forests, and high rates of sedimentation that opened up new mudflats for colonization. Now Gunn is out , and Skydance (the company formed by the merger of Warner and Paramount) is already dismantling his grand plans for the DCU. That means that Man of Tomorrow, which arrives next summer, will be the final entry in Gunn's ambitious, and occasionally divisive, DC experiment. The DCU's first chapter — officially titled 'Gods and Monsters' — gave us Supergirl and Clayface (as well as TV shows like Peacemaker S2 and Lanterns ) in the run-up to Clark Kent and Lex Luthor 's return. Man of Tomorrow looks to be upping the stakes from Earthly villains to intergalactic baddies with the introduction of Brainiac, and it may well have been the herald of the first Justice League movie in the rebooted DCU. Gunn has yet to prove audiences actually care about more than Batman and Supes, which might explain why this follow-up is also an ensemble of sorts. science.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
science.description: A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered. When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices. Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days. "For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis," Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville said in a statement . Several other supernova imposters have been observed over the past decade or two. Until now, no one knew what causes these stars to repeatedly cry wolf. Thanks to Chandra ’s X-ray vision, Aghakhanloo has led a team of astronomers who think they have now uncovered an explanation. How did a cosmic vampire hide as a supernova? The supernova imposter is named AT 2016blu, and is a type of star that we call a 'luminous blue variable,' or LBV. These are the most massive and luminous stars in the universe and their extreme characteristics result in them being highly unstable, undergoing intermittent bouts of mass loss as they eject material from their outer layers into the surrounding space. However, faking a supernova is not part of their typical behavior, so a new way of looking at AT 2016blu was needed. "To understand the cause of these eruptions, we realized that we needed X-ray data that was timed so that we’d observe the star when it was in an outburst," team member Núria Torres-Albà, also from the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, said. Aghakhanloo’s team were granted the opportunity to commandeer Chandra to target an outburst of AT 2016blu at the earliest opportunity. That opportunity arose in March 2026. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/University of Virginia/M. Aghakhanloo et al; Optical: NSF/KAIT.) Chandra had previously and coincidentally looked in the direction of NGC 4559 back in 2001 and 2002 and did not notice anything unusual back then. This time around, however, it captured a powerful blast of X-rays coinciding with yet another false supernova outburst. The X-ray detection allowed Aghakhanloo’s team to assemble a picture of what is happening. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years
science.description: null On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P . To say it was a bumpy landing would be an understatement. The European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014. It was supposed to use harpoons to secure itself on to the surface of Comet 67P, but the harpoons never fired. When it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space . The first bounce brought Philae half a mile above the comet's surface before gravity brought it back down. Philae was missing for almost two years before scientists found it . Images from Rosetta showed Philae stuck in a dark crevice on top of the rubber duck-shaped comet. The European Space Agency's Rosetta spacecraft captured these photos of the Philae lander descending toward, and then bouncing off, the surface of Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko during its historic touchdown on Nov. 12, 2014. (Image credit: ESA/Rosetta/MPS for OSIRIS Team MPS/UPD/LAM/IAA/SSO/INTA/UPM/DASP/IDA) Why it mattered The European Space Agency 's Rosetta and Philae expedition was a first-of-its-kind mission, an endeavour to not just rendezvous with a comet and watch it change over time as it approached the sun (that was Rosetta's job), but also to soft-land a probe on its icy and rocky surface to see what a comet is truly made of. The Rosetta and Philae mission succeeded on both counts, but Philae's historic landing was marred by its turbulent touchdown. Philae actually landed three different times on Comet 67/P , all because the harpoons designed to secure it in place didn't fire as planned. After the first landing, Philae bounced up and drifted around the comet for two hours, making another bounce before Rosetta's cameras lost track of it. Scientists figured it was stuck in a shady spot where sunlight couldn't reach its solar panels. Because it was solar-powered, Philae needed to be facing the sun properly to generate enough power for sustained operation on the comet's surface. Still, Philae did have some power stored in batteries, which lasted for more than two days on the surface. That allowed Philae to perform some science with its 10 instruments in the time it had on Comet 67/P. Most notably, Philae found organic molecules that had never been detected on a comet before. The Rosetta orbiter continued to orbit Comet 67P until September 2016, and it was in that month -- just weeks before Rosetta itself landed on the comet on Sept. 30, 2016 -- that the spacecraft rediscovered the Philae lander lying on its side in a rocky crevice. Will you be able to spot its leviathan upper stage, known as Ship, or its Starlink satellite passengers as they circle Earth during the historic orbital jaunt? Flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT) on Nov. 13 . Starship will fly from SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas, where it will be 4:45 p.m. at the opening of the window — about an hour before sunset. The launch could therefore be especially dramatic for folks in the area. "As it launches towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S. are going to be in Texas and the states along the Gulf of Mexico," Robert Massey, deputy executive director at the Royal Astronomical Society, told Space.com. "They could see the exhaust plume (the ' jellyfish ') with the sky darker for observers further east." If all goes to plan, Starship's Super Heavy booster will propel the Ship upper stage through the densest part of Earth's atmosphere before returning to Starbase for a powered landing and capture via the "chopstick" arms of the "Mechazilla" tower system . Ship, meanwhile, will go on to orbit Earth approximately 14 times over the following 22 hours, during which time it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before returning to Starbase for its own ambitious catch attempt. When should I look for Starship and its Starlink train? Satellite visibility in the night sky depends on a cocktail of factors, from the size of the spacecraft to its reflectivity, orbital inclination and position relative to the Earth and sun. science.title: 'Warhammer Survivors' is the perfect gateway into the 40K universe
science.description: We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd. Warhammer Survivors changes that, finally providing curious gamers with an easy entry point into the grim darkness of the 41st millennium. Developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this new spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe. This means heroes and enemies from all over the Warhammer mythos meet together in a bite-sized game that anyone can figure out and enjoy in less than five minutes. When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into . Warhammer Survivors isn't bogged down by dense lore, involved mechanics, or massive campaign playthroughs. It's more of an "inspired by" effort that gives casuals a small taste of the series' iconic characters — including Boltgun 's Malum Caedo — and factions like the terrifying Tyranids, the raucous Orks, and the foul forces of Chaos. All of 40K's (and Age of Sigmar's) recognizable elements are on display, but they serve more as flavoring sprinkled on top of Vampire Survivors' successful formula. If you're new to the Survivors-like subgenre, it's a unique gaming experience. You battle an endless onslaught of enemies that slowly march towards you, with your character passively attacking automatically. You only need to move them around sprawling arenas and select level-up upgrades and items after collecting enough gems (skulls in this case). The moment-to-moment gameplay is as simple as it can get outside of walking sims and interactive "experiences," but there's a deceiving depth to item synergies and how to correctly "build" characters to endure all the carnage. Unlike Poncle's original game, Warhammer Survivors struggles a bit to get going. The early hours are sluggish until you unlock certain meta upgrades, but its still got that Vampire Survivors magic at its core. As far as "podcast/gym games" go, this is a perfect fit. There's just enough going on to keep one's brain engaged, but minimal inputs and a tight overarching design lead to a rhythm that's easy to get into without using much brainpower. It's oddly satisfying to weave through enemies and level up your firepower, watching a single Astra Militarum grunt grow into a full Lasgun-spamming, chainsword-wielding wrecking ball. Achievement and unlock hunters will find enough to bite into here, too. It's unclear if the devs will continue to add more Warhammer 40K and Age of Sigmar deep cuts to this game via DLCs and free updates, but those universes have daunting depths to explore. This really could become a gateway game for future 40K fans: by the time they realize they're hooked, they'll already have 2000 pts of space marines painted and ready to play. The summit’s joint hosts, Turkey and Australia, are pushing for a clean energy revolution, but this week Turkey announced two new oilfields that would help boost production 30 per cent, while promising to double natural gas production. science.title: Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video)
science.description: null On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter , the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy , the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe. The new data release, designated DR1-Foundation, was built from 13 months of observations and is accompanied by a multitude of images, including large sky mosaics. It marks the first major release of mission data since Euclid launched in mid-2023 . The core of the Messier 81 galaxy group as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) "These are far more than beautiful pictures; today marks a scientific milestone in our study of the cosmos," ESA's Director of Science, Carole Mundell said in a statement . "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy and demonstrating the excellence of European technology, science and international collaboration." What's in the Euclid release The ESA put into raw numbers the sheer number of celestial objects viewed by the Dark Universe Detective and contained in DR1-Foundation. That includes light spectra from 160 million sources, over 900 million galaxies, and 60 million candidates for quasars , regions of space dominated by feeding supermassive black holes . "This is a change in scale from Euclid's previous releases, which included a few days of observations over around 60 degrees squared of sky," ESA's Euclid project scientist Valeria Pettorino said. "We're now releasing more than a year of data covering a significantly larger area. This unlocks groundbreaking science." science.title: Pakistani astronaut set to become 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station this month
science.description: null An astronaut from Pakistan is set to launch on China's Shenzhou 24 mission in the coming weeks and become the first-ever international visitor to the Tiangong space station. A pair of astronaut candidates from Pakistan have been training at the Astronaut Centre of China in Beijing, following an agreement reached between China and Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 and a subsequent selection process. China's human spaceflight agency confirmed in a Nov. 7 press statement that the upcoming Shenzhou 24 mission will carry one of the astronauts. The agency also released a mission patch . "China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Nov. 9. "Having the Pakistani astronaut on board China's spaceships will mark the first-ever joint mission of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program." It is not yet known which of the two candidates will fly on Shenzhou 24. They were named in Pakistani press reports as Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, both pilots from the country's military forces. The pair were chosen from a wider pool of around 20 finalists. The chosen candidate will fly as a payload specialist on Shenzhou 24 along with two Chinese colleagues, while the other will be on standby as a backup. While the Chinese astronauts will be starting a six-month-long stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will spend roughly a week in orbit aboard Tiangong during a standard crew rotation period. He will then return to Earth aboard the departing Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, along with two Chinese astronauts who will have completed a six-month-long stay in orbit. The arrangement means changes to China's usual "three in, three out" Tiangong crew rotations. One of the three Shenzhou 23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong on May 24, will stay aboard and complete China's first-ever year-long stay in orbit, while the Pakistani astronaut will take their seat aboard Shenzhou 23 to return home. During his stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will be responsible for four research payloads selected from more than 300 proposals, according to Pakistan's space agency, SUPARCO. China has not announced a timeline for the launch of the Shenzhou 24 mission, but it is expected to lift off before the end of November. The Shenzhou 23 astronauts currently aboard Tiangong are closing in on 180 days in orbit, nearing an end to their six months in space. Shenzhou 24 will launch from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in the Gobi Desert on a Long March 2F rocket.
